Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, the inherited rollout evidence, and both policy-relevant skills. I’ll use the fish-control shelf for the required structured transfer and inspect both wake views before choosing the single candidate.

The contract confirms there is one editable solver file, no local CFD run is allowed, and the candidate is not complete until both provenance notes and durable guidance change. I’m now anchoring the visual comparison to the scores, metrics, diagnostics, inherited notes, and current controller before consulting transfer primitives.

The two-view sheets and telemetry agree: all four policies self-propel through still water with the same coherent alternating wake and late hook; none show numerical instability or actuator contacts. The meaningful contrast is subtle middle/late-course allocation—course-priority suppression arrives earliest (26.2405T) but raises peak yaw moment slightly, while carrier relief is slower and translation-consistent line-of-sight selection is nearly tied. I’m now consulting the shelf for one invariant that can address this course/line-of-sight conflict without retuning the proven gait.

The shelf reinforces a minimal-intervention principle: preserve the proven traveling bend and modulate only the steering residual from reliable feedback. I’m selecting one candidate mechanism—a reflection-equivariant course-consistency projection that smoothly suppresses only a history-based line-of-sight correction when observable body-frame translation says it points the wrong way. It removes the arbitrary distance corridor from the successful course-priority test and leaves agreement, low-speed states, redirect, propulsion, and all viability guards unchanged.

The candidate and durable guidance are now updated. I’m validating the public contract, parameter schema, reflection symmetry, bounded outputs, and the intended “only conflicting residual changes” behavior with deterministic state tests; this is policy-only validation, not CFD.

Local checks pass: notes/guidance are materially updated, the policy contract is finite and bounded, reflection equivariance holds, agreement and zero-speed cases are exact pass-throughs, conflict states change only the intended anterior residual, and the solver boundary is clean. I’m invoking the required independent check-runner now; it will repeat the non-CFD contract, guidance, and boundary checks.

The configured checker could not start because its pinned mini model is unavailable in this account context. I’ve already run its exact commands locally; I’m retrying the same independent, non-editing audit with the available default checker so the required validation still has a second pass.

The independent fallback checker passed all three required checks and made no edits: guidance provenance, Julia policy contract, and solver boundary are all clean. The configured checker’s launch failure was tooling-only; its exact audit has now passed twice, once locally and once independently.

Implemented exactly one policy candidate: a course-consistency projection that suppresses only line-of-sight steering residuals conflicting with observable body-frame course. The proven gait, redirect, posterior modulation, and viability guards remain unchanged.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md)

The notes include the required structured bookshelf transfer and falsification criteria. Contract, schema, symmetry, bounded-output, guidance, and boundary checks all pass independently. No CFD was run; EvE will evaluate the candidate after exit.
